## What I did

AI summary for now, I will write this properly soon

<!-- Briefly describe what your PR does -->
This pull request introduces the foundation for "Ghost Stories," an experimental feature for automated story discovery and testing, primarily targeting React projects using the Vitest addon. The changes add a new event-driven channel for orchestrating story discovery and testing, update the test plugin logic to support this flow, and introduce error categorization utilities with comprehensive tests. Additionally, new core events and wiring are added to support the feature.

**Ghost Stories feature integration:**

* Added a new `ghost-stories-channel` (`initGhostStoriesChannel`) that listens for `GHOST_STORIES_REQUEST` events, discovers component candidates, runs tests on generated stories, records telemetry, and emits a response event. This is currently gated to React projects with the Vitest addon. (`code/core/src/core-server/server-channel/ghost-stories-channel.ts`)
* Registered the new Ghost Stories channel in the server initialization logic, ensuring it is set up alongside other server channels. (`code/core/src/core-server/presets/common-preset.ts`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6f9af3b0651245cd00c4c837f2a699d9a14353d6c8f8281432f658e518475288R35) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6f9af3b0651245cd00c4c837f2a699d9a14353d6c8f8281432f658e518475288R264)

**Core events and plugin wiring:**

* Added new core events: `GHOST_STORIES_REQUEST` and `GHOST_STORIES_RESPONSE`, and exported them for use in the system. (`code/core/src/core-events/index.ts`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6a200b958b24141a32f13ee1454fdb0f81dfee469f6da8abe898c63ae8c9ddc7R91-R93) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6a200b958b24141a32f13ee1454fdb0f81dfee469f6da8abe898c63ae8c9ddc7R165-R166)
* Updated the Vitest plugin to recognize when Ghost Stories is enabled via environment variables, and to set a `ghostStories` global. This disables certain tests when Ghost Stories are running and ensures only relevant files are transformed. (`code/addons/vitest/src/vitest-plugin/index.ts`, `code/addons/a11y/src/preview.tsx`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0b850fef5ef3e7b1f898b7559fb2bdfbdc757ecdf933ec31ab175038816af7ceL104-L130) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0b850fef5ef3e7b1f898b7559fb2bdfbdc757ecdf933ec31ab175038816af7ceL345-R334) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0b850fef5ef3e7b1f898b7559fb2bdfbdc757ecdf933ec31ab175038816af7ceL369-R369) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-5f51b6995a8edbc26c94cfcb8ef84c961ef0e6e4b17c5a9f626432159354eaa5R20-R23)

**Error analysis utilities:**

* Added a utility and comprehensive test suite for categorizing and aggregating errors from automated story tests, enabling better diagnostics and telemetry for common provider and render errors. (`code/core/src/core-server/utils/ghost-stories/categorize-render-errors.test.ts`)

comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🔴 Critical_

**Critical: Mock path does not match the import path.**

The mock targets `'../utils/ghost-stories/story-generation'` but the actual module imported at line 67 is `'../utils/ghost-stories/get-candidates'`. This mismatch means `getComponentCandidates` won't be mocked, causing tests to call the real implementation.


<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-vi.mock('../utils/ghost-stories/story-generation', async (importOriginal) => {
+vi.mock('../utils/ghost-stories/get-candidates', async (importOriginal) => {
   const actual = await importOriginal<typeof import('../utils/ghost-stories/get-candidates')>();
   return {
     ...actual,
     getComponentCandidates: vi.fn(),
   };
 });
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In @code/core/src/core-server/server-channel/ghost-stories-channel.test.ts
around lines 32 - 38, The test mock targets the wrong module, so
getComponentCandidates isn't being mocked; update the vi.mock call to target the
same module that's imported in the test and use the same module type in
importOriginal, then return a mock implementation for getComponentCandidates.
Specifically, change the vi.mock target to the module that exports
getComponentCandidates, adjust the importOriginal generic to that same module,
and keep returning {...actual, getComponentCandidates: vi.fn()} so tests use the
mocked getComponentCandidates.
```

</details>
